save_card.title: THIRD-DEGREE AV BLOCK (SPLIT)
items: P waves march on their own clock
QRS march on their own slow clock
The PR is never the same

memory_line: Third-degree AV block (SPLIT): the top and bottom beat apart.
caption_lesson:
✅ First, normal sinus rhythm
• Every P wave is followed by a QRS after the same short pause (PR 0.12 to 0.20 seconds)
• The AV (atrioventricular) node passes every signal

🧱 Then third-degree AV block (SPLIT), also called complete heart block
1️⃣ The AV node blocks EVERY signal. The atria (upper chambers) keep firing on time
2️⃣ A backup pacemaker below the block takes over, slowly: 40 to 60 from the junction (narrow QRS) or 20 to 40 from the ventricles (wide QRS)
3️⃣ Top and bottom SPLIT: P waves and QRS each march on their own clock. The PR changes every beat
4️⃣ Too slow to hold the BP (blood pressure). Dizziness, fainting, and the backup can fail

⚡ What to do
• Check her: pulse, BP, how she looks
• Pads on now. Atropine may be ordered first, but it often fails in third-degree block, so be ready for transcutaneous pacing (through the skin), as ordered
• Call now. A permanent pacemaker is the usual fix

rn_checks: Third-degree AV block: no atrial impulses conduct; atria and ventricles independent (AV dissociation); PR varies; P waves march through
Escape rates: junctional 40 to 60 with a narrow QRS; ventricular 20 to 40 with a wide QRS
